"That is, when RDF documents with blank nodes are added to fedora, those blank nodes would remain anonymous and not be made available at any skolemized location."

is inaccurate. In fact, the incoming bnodes will certainly be skolemized (there is no other way to persist them) but the skolemized URIs will not be exposed via the Fedora/LDP API. There is no meaning in the idea of a "skolemized location".
"The fedora:Blanknode class in the fedora ontology would be eliminated."
Yes, but to be clear, there will continue to exist a repository-internal type for distinguishing the skolem nodes.

The magic number has to do with ModeShape implementation checking node permissions a certain number of times when updating and setting properties.So it should be safe to change it to the new number, but it might be much better to get rid of (or at least modify) those lines altogether since the checks are too implementation dependent. Just to clarify, I didn't introduce these checks (only updated them to keep the status quo).

However, what exactly ModeShape is doing under the covers is of less importance... and apparently evolving with incremental ModeShape releases. I would suggest changing the tests to ensure that `hasPermission()` is being called at least once (i.e. count > 0).
More granularity than that is brittle and meaningless.

I have poked a bit at this issue and made some small progress. The issue that I am seeing is that deskolemization is happening during RDF updates (PUT and PATCH), and causing two issues:
1) Blank node identifiers are rejected by the JcrPropertyStatementListener as "not being in the domain"
2) In RDF updates, provided blank nodes are not able to match with existing blank nodes which are deskolemized.
The following PR appears to address the PATCH scenario, as detailed below, without any apparent ill effect.
Where "bnode.txt" and "bnode-update.txt" are the same as

In general, it seems that if we limited the deskolemization to RdfStreams that are being returned to the client, then all should be well. The issue comes when we deskolemize resources internally while trying to perform update operations.
The reason I deskolemized for updates is so that SPARQL Update would work properly. (Which it does to create new bnodes, but not otherwise.)
I don't see how we can avoid deskolemizing if we want to use SPARQL Update.
Interesting. What I am seeing is that sparql-update only works with PR-786.
, could you add a sparql-update integration test, possibly mimicking the scenario
It must be testing a different scenario, because it passes before and after PR-786.
and I detail above as another integration test.
Yes, that's my point. It works to
bnodes, but not to modify them.
blank nodes that is the problem. (Which appears as a problem modifying them because SPARQL Update's version of modification is removal-and-then-insertion of triples.)

Because the mapping between RDF resources and Fedora resources (as represented in IdentifierConverter and its subtypes) is one-in-one-out, it's not possible to determine, given a blank node to be removed, which Skolem node should be removed.

This is obviously a solvable problem, and we'd have to look at the various techniques that actual triplestores have used to solve it. I'm in no position to dedicate that time, and I doubt anyone else is. As predicted, attempting to deal with blank nodes is going to slowly turn Fedora into a shoddy triplestore.
All updates reverted with merged PR-788
This task is to re-implement blank nodes along the lines of the following plan:
1) The REST API would continue to accept RDF documents with blank nodes (this is not a change from the current behavior).
2) The fedora:Blanknode class in the fedora ontology would be eliminated.
3) Blank nodes will no longer be published at the .well-known/genid location.

That is, when RDF documents with blank nodes are added to Fedora, those blank nodes will be skolemized internally and stored under the node that the RDF document described, but will not be made available at any location.
4) When fedora:Container nodes are requested, any skolem nodes contained in that document will be serialized as blank nodes, according to the concrete RDF syntax that is requested.
5) When a fedora:Container (one that contains blank nodes) is deleted, the corresponding skolem nodes will also be removed from Fedora.

In general, it seems that if we limited the deskolemization to RdfStreams that are being returned to the client, then all should be well. The issue comes when we deskolemize resources internally while trying to perform update operations.

The reason I deskolemized for updates is so that SPARQL Update would work properly. (Which it does to create new bnodes, but not otherwise.)

I don't see how we can avoid deskolemizing if we want to use SPARQL Update.
Interesting. What I am seeing is that sparql-update only works with PR-786. A. Soroka, could you add a sparql-update integration test, possibly mimicking the scenario Unknown and I detail above?

It's already there.

org.fcrepo.integration.http.api.FedoraLdpIT.testPatchWithBlankNode()

It must be testing a different scenario, because it passes before and after PR-786.
We should add the scenario Unknown and I detail above as another integration test.
Yes, that's my point. It works to create bnodes, but not to modify them.

On closer inspection, it's actually removing blank nodes that is the problem. (Which appears as a problem modifying them because SPARQL Update's version of modification is removal-and-then-insertion of triples.)

Because the mapping between RDF resources and Fedora resources (as represented in IdentifierConverter and its subtypes) is one-in-one-out, it's not possible to determine, given a blank node to be removed, which Skolem node should be removed.

This is obviously a solvable problem, and we'd have to look at the various techniques that actual triplestores have used to solve it. I'm in no position to dedicate that time, and I doubt anyone else is. As predicted, attempting to deal with blank nodes is going to slowly turn Fedora into a shoddy triplestore.

This task is to re-implement blank nodes along the lines of the following plan:

1) The REST API would continue to accept RDF documents with blank nodes (this is not a change from the current behavior).

2) The fedora:Blanknode class in the fedora ontology would be eliminated.

3) Blank nodes will no longer be published at the .well-known/genid location.

That is, when RDF documents with blank nodes are added to Fedora, those blank nodes will be skolemized internally and stored under the node that the RDF document described, but will not be made available at any location.

4) When fedora:Container nodes are requested, any skolem nodes contained in that document will be serialized as blank nodes, according to the concrete RDF syntax that is requested.

5) When a fedora:Container (one that contains blank nodes) is deleted, the corresponding skolem nodes will also be removed from Fedora.
